This state/province was the first in the country to reintroduce religious criminal law - its religious establishment law was introduced on 27 October 1999 and came into force on 27 January 2000 - triggering a cascade of eleven more belt states by 2002. Religious-morality police activity is documented here, and a foreign government's religious-freedom commission's 2019 implementation study covers this state alongside two others using 2017 case data, confirming operational religious-court function. No trans-specific incident or capital sentence is recorded for this unit.

The enacted religious framework, documented morality-police presence, and case-level study coverage are the unit's distinguishing facts; its trigger role makes it the origin point of the belt as a whole.
